title: Release playbook drift and rollback scribe
body:
Meeting date: 2026-03-08
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha P., Miguel S., Lauren K., Benji R., Priya D., Samir (on call), Chelsea (notes)

Purpose: quick weekly sync focused on observed divergences between the documented release playbook and how teams actually run release trains / hotfixes. Capture concrete rollback friction points and surface fixes we can reasonably ship this quarter.

High-level summary:
- We saw 3 small production degradations in the last 6 weeks tied to procedural drift rather than code regressions.
- Primary themes: inconsistent canary gating, manual overrides bypassing automated fallout paths, and undocumented pre-warm steps for quantized models (KV cache warm-up).
- Goal: reduce human-in-the-loop rollback time by 50% for high-severity events via playbook clarifications and light automation.

Context / background notes:
- Teams running rapid weekly release trains have adapted shortcuts (local scripts, ad-hoc labels) that are not reflected in the canonical playbook. This was helpful for speed but increased mean time to safe rollback during two incidents.
- We need to balance velocity with predictable fallbacks: add explicit exemptions in playbook for valid shortcuts, plus automated guardrails for common footguns.

Observed playbook drift (concrete examples):
1) Canary gating mismatch
   - Doc: canary passes when p95 latency and error budget thresholds met for 60m.
   - Reality: mobile team runs a 15m canary to iterate faster and manually approves via Slack reactions.
   - Risk: short canaries missed slowly-accumulating resource trends (e.g. KV miss amplification).
   - Note: we saw this on RE-2107 (latency creep post-deploy).

2) KV-cache pre-warm not consistently executed for quantized variants
   - Doc: models that use on-start warmup must run KV seeding in warmup script.
   - Reality: some infra / private deploys used image baking with lazy-warm path, relying on traffic to fill KV cache; for quantized models this led to immediate 10-30% p95 spikes under first traffic.
   - Impact: customer-facing latency blips and aborted canary rollouts.

3) Manual hotfix bypasses going straight to prod
   - Pattern: when on-call busy, engineers occasionally skip staging & roll forward a hotfix directly to prod using a pre-approved service account.
   - Doc: emergency hotfixes allowed but require post-deploy audit and automated smoke tests.
   - Drift: smoke tests sometimes omitted if CI tokens not available.

4) Autoscale hysteresis and scaling thresholds changed locally
   - Several teams adjusted autoscaler thresholds to avoid flapping. Those local changes were not communicated and conflict with RCA telemetry assumptions.

Incident vignette (short timeline):
- 2026-02-28 hotfix attempt for model A (RE-2123): attempted canary for quantized-8 variant. Canary window set to 15m due to deploy constraints. 3m after traffic cut, p95 increased 28% due to cold KV misses. Team manually aborted but rollback script required manual credential fetch and took ~26 minutes.
- Root cause: two-fold: shorter canary + no pre-warm for quantized image + hard-to-run rollback steps.

Decisions / proposals from meeting:
1) Add a "safe-short-canary" pattern to playbook
   - Definition: allowed 15m canary only if an automated KV-warm step and smoke-sanity check pass before routing production traffic.
   - Implementation: small Python utility (warm-kv) that runs against canary instances. PR in repo: PR/452 (linked above).

2) Rollback safe-mode checklist (formalize, then automate where possible)
   - Minimum viable rollback checklist to live in the release tool UI:
     * verify on-call owner and emergency-credential status
     * run automated smoke tests (tokenized) with 2-minute timeout
     * trigger immediate routing to fallback model variant (model-baker-2)
     * notify Slack #incidents with automated payload
     * enable degraded-L7 throttling policy for 10m
   - If any step fails, escalate automatically to SRE pager.

3) Enforce smoke test pass as gating for hotfix prod path
   - Hotfix endpoints will reject direct-to-prod unless smoke test artifacts exist (CI artifact ID). Temporary exception allowed but auto-expiring and auditable.

4) Autoscaler changes must be in a short RFC and tagged in deployment metadata
   - Add "scaler-note" label to release metadata and require minimal rationale. We will surface any unlabeled changes in weekly checks.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Miguel S.: prototype warm-kv utility and add to release-playbook repo; demo by 2026-03-18. (JIRA: RE-2198)
- Lauren K.: modify release UI to require smoke-artifact id for hotfix-to-prod path; rollout feature flag by 2026-03-25. (JIRA: RE-2203)
- Benji R.: create a short RFC template for autoscaler changes and publish on Confluence; done by 2026-03-15.
- Priya D.: write the rollback safe-mode checklist into the canonical playbook and own the first runbook test; checklist live draft by 2026-03-11.
- Aisha P.: run a 1-hour tabletop drill with on-call rotation next week (2026-03-15) focusing on quantized model no-warm scenario; capture timings.

Notes on automation tradeoffs:
- We intentionally avoid fully automatic rollbacks for now because of false-positive surface area (noisy telemetries). Instead: reduce manual steps, improve reliability of gate artifacts, and add a low-friction operator-confirm step where needed.

Quick wins (can ship within 2 weeks):
- Add a one-click smoke-test runner in the release UI (Lauren to prototype).
- Bake a small pre-warm hook into the image startup script for quantized models (Miguel to prototype).
- Add a required "hotfix-reason" short freeform field so audits are less noisy (low effort).

Metrics to track (for next 6 weeks):
- Mean time to rollback (target: down 50% from current baseline of ~22min)
- Fraction of hotfixes that follow gated path vs direct-to-prod (target: >95% gated)
- Number of canary rollbacks due to KV-cold misses (target: 0 after warm-kv rollout)

Unresolved / open questions:
- How do we handle private/on-prem deployments that cannot call centralized warm-kv due to networking constraints? (Priya to propose option of offline warm artifact).
- Is the additional gating materially slowing urgent rollouts? We will measure via tabletop drill; if it is, explore "one-button bypass" with stricter post-deploy audits.

Reference snippets (to paste into playbook):
- "Safe short-canary pattern": must include a KV-warm step + smoke sanity check before any traffic is routed.
- Rollback checklist (short): 1) stop new canary traffic 2) execute rollback script (credentials cached) 3) route to fallback variant 4) notify incident channel 5) begin degraded throttling policy.

Next sync: 2026-03-15 (tabletop drill).

Notes to self / scribbles (informal):
- Samir mentioned a local script (bin/fast-rollback) that still requires human token fetch. Need to either wrap with token-cache or mark as deprecated.
- Priya: we should publish a one-page "release emergency crib sheet" for new hires; quick wins for pager training.
- Ask growth team whether they can schedule non-customer-facing internal traffic spikes for warmup tests (avoid interfering with experiments).

Attachments / artifacts to add to the canonical playbook after edits:
- warm-kv README & sample run command
- rollback-checklist.md
- RFC template for autoscaler changes

End of note.

[informal comment section below — not part of the formal playbook yet] 
- Lauren: "If we can get the smoke-runner to 90% reliability, I think we can make the gated path the default for pretty much everything."
- Miguel: "warm-kv prototype will probably be ~200 LOC, simple HTTP pinger + KV seed script; we can iterate."
summary: Working notes capturing playbook drift observed in recent releases, incident vignette and proposed mitigations (warm-kv, smoke gating, rollback checklist). Action items assigned with short ETAs. Planned tabletop on 2026-03-15.
